variables.physical_definition: Side length of the square duct (characteristic length scale)
Dynamic viscosity of the fluid (viscous momentum diffusivity parameter)
Proportionality coefficient relating electric field to current density in the fluid via E = eta * J
Applied pressure gradient (pressure change per unit length)
Magnetic flux density (magnitude of applied magnetic field)

h.aliases: duct side length; side length of square duct
h.definition: Side length of a square duct cross-section.
h.ambiguity_notes: The symbol h is also used for channel half-height or full container height; all are length quantities.
h.source: MHD Flow in Simple Cubic Periodic Array Geometry, Journal of Fusion Energy (2023)

h.definition: Distance from a channel wall to its centerline for a symmetric plane channel.
h.ambiguity_notes: The symbol h is also used for full height, enthalpy, or heat-transfer coefficient in other contexts.
h.source: Wall-bounded turbulence literature defining friction Reynolds number and viscous scaling

h.definition: Heat flux divided by a driving temperature difference.
h.ambiguity_notes: h is also used for length or enthalpy in some contexts.
h.source: Lupi, Heat Transfer, in Fundamentals of Electroheat

mu.aliases: absolute viscosity; viscosity coefficient; dynamic viscosity coefficient
mu.definition: Coefficient relating Newtonian viscous shear stress to velocity gradient.
mu.ambiguity_notes: Symbols eta/η can instead denote electrical resistivity, magnetic diffusivity, or other quantities; symbols mu/μ are also used for magnetic permeability in some contexts.
mu.source: NIST SP 811, Guide for the Use of the International System of Units (SI)

mu.aliases: resistivity; specific electrical resistance; rho notation for electrical resistivity; ρ notation for electrical resistivity
mu.definition: Material property relating electric field to current density; equivalently electrical resistance times a length scale divided by area.
mu.ambiguity_notes: Eta/η may denote dynamic viscosity or magnetic diffusivity; rho/ρ may denote mass density. In an MHD prompt explicitly saying electrical resistivity, use this record.
mu.source: MHD Flow in Simple Cubic Periodic Array Geometry, Journal of Fusion Energy (2023)

mu.definition: Constitutive coefficient relating magnetic flux density and magnetic field strength in a linear medium.
mu.ambiguity_notes: The symbol mu/μ is also the standard symbol for dynamic viscosity in fluid mechanics.

rho.aliases: density; fluid density; material density; wall density
rho.ambiguity_notes: The symbol rho/ρ may also denote electrical resistivity in electromagnetism; resolve by physical context.

rho.aliases: resistivity; specific electrical resistance; rho notation for electrical resistivity; ρ notation for electrical resistivity
rho.definition: Material property relating electric field to current density; equivalently electrical resistance times a length scale divided by area.
rho.ambiguity_notes: Eta/η may denote dynamic viscosity or magnetic diffusivity; rho/ρ may denote mass density. In an MHD prompt explicitly saying electrical resistivity, use this record.
rho.source: MHD Flow in Simple Cubic Periodic Array Geometry, Journal of Fusion Energy (2023)

rho.definition: Constitutive coefficient relating magnetic flux density and magnetic field strength in a linear medium.
rho.ambiguity_notes: The symbol mu/μ is also the standard symbol for dynamic viscosity in fluid mechanics.

eta.aliases: absolute viscosity; viscosity coefficient; dynamic viscosity coefficient
eta.definition: Coefficient relating Newtonian viscous shear stress to velocity gradient.
eta.ambiguity_notes: Symbols eta/η can instead denote electrical resistivity, magnetic diffusivity, or other quantities; symbols mu/μ are also used for magnetic permeability in some contexts.
eta.source: NIST SP 811, Guide for the Use of the International System of Units (SI)

eta.aliases: resistivity; specific electrical resistance; rho notation for electrical resistivity; ρ notation for electrical resistivity
eta.definition: Material property relating electric field to current density; equivalently electrical resistance times a length scale divided by area.
eta.ambiguity_notes: Eta/η may denote dynamic viscosity or magnetic diffusivity; rho/ρ may denote mass density. In an MHD prompt explicitly saying electrical resistivity, use this record.
eta.source: MHD Flow in Simple Cubic Periodic Array Geometry, Journal of Fusion Energy (2023)

eta.definition: Twice the component of rotation normal to the local horizontal plane.
eta.source: Hauke, An Introduction to Fluid Mechanics and Transport Phenomena

dp_dx.aliases: applied pressure gradient; streamwise pressure gradient; pressure drop per unit length

B.definition: Magnetic flux per unit area; the quantity whose SI unit is tesla.
B.ambiguity_notes: Many fluid and engineering papers informally call B the magnetic field. Distinguish B from magnetic field strength H, whose SI unit is A m^-1.

B.definition: Amount of solute divided by mass of solvent.

The KB record pq_dynamic_viscosity defines dynamic viscosity (symbols μ or eta) with SI dimensions M L^-1 T^-1, i.e. M=1, L=-1, T=-1 and zeros elsewhere. This matches the candidate exponents and applies because μ is explicitly the viscous coefficient in the fluid mechanics portion of the MHD problem, not magnetic permeability (which is a different KB entry).

ρ is stated as the fluid mass density. The KB record pq_mass_density defines mass density with SI dimensions M L^-3 (M=1, L=-3) and zeros for other base dimensions. This record directly matches the physical role of ρ in the problem (mass per unit volume), so the candidate vector is correct.

The problem explicitly defines η via E = η J (electric field equals η times current density), which is the constitutive relation for electrical resistivity in MHD. KB record pq_electrical_resistivity gives SI dimensions M L^3 T^-3 I^-2 (i.e. I=-2, L=3, M=1, T=-3), matching the candidate. pq_dynamic_viscosity is cited only to note the common symbol ambiguity (η sometimes denotes viscosity), but the provided definition in the problem selects electrical resistivity unambiguously, so the resistivity record is the applicable KB record.

dp/dx is defined as the applied pressure gradient (pressure change per unit length). KB record pq_pressure_gradient supplies SI dimensions M L^-2 T^-2 (M=1, L=-2, T=-2) which match the candidate. pq_mean_flow_velocity is included to show the context (pressure gradient drives mean flow) but the pressure-gradient record is the direct dimensional match and applies here.

B is given as the magnetic flux density (magnitude of the applied magnetic field). The KB record pq_magnetic_flux_density defines B with SI dimensions M T^-2 I^-1 (M=1, T=-2, I=-1, L=0), which matches the candidate exponents. This record is directly applicable because the problem uses B as the magnetic induction acting on the conducting fluid in MHD.

model_messages.content: Audit every named physical input in this exact typed ledger, including literal SI coordinate values. Do not substitute the correct definition or a KB vector for a wrong candidate and then claim PASSED. Return ledger_sha256 and each csv_name exactly once; before_si_exponents must copy the actual candidate. PASSED confirms the actual vector, CONFLICT requires a complete corrected suggested vector, and UNCERTAIN does not permit numerical execution. KB_RECORD requires actual entry_id citations from that variable's retrieved records. Canonical entity names are read by the program from the selected IDs; do not echo another quantity-name field. Your reason must explain why each cited record applies to this variable in the original problem, not merely why its vector matches. Cited vectors must support all known coordinates of the proposed/confirmed SI vector. INTERNAL_REASONING uses no IDs and must explain the physical meaning. Retrieval rank is relevance, not truth. Resolve symbol ambiguity from the original problem; do not choose an unrelated matching symbol. Known absent base dimensions must be explicit '0'; null means genuinely unknown, not unused. If any current coordinate is unknown, request revision or report UNCERTAIN; never call a partly known vector PASSED. Give a complete correction when physically justified. If a correction remains partly unknown, preserve null and explain what remains unresolved; the program will request revision rather than invent zeros. Lack of KB alone is not a physical contradiction. Matrix compilation and n/r/k are program tasks, not audit tasks.
